# 4 Maccabees Chapter 9 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Sinaiticus) | **Section:** The First Brothers Tortured and Killed

---

**9:1** When Antiochus was convinced that he had been defeated by their refusal, he ordered the instruments of torture to be brought.

**9:2** When the rack and the other implements of torture had been brought, the tyrant ordered that the tongue of their spokesman should be cut out and that he should be scalped and his hands and feet cut off, while the other brothers and the mother watched.

**9:3** When he had been thus mutilated in all his limbs, Antiochus commanded that he should be brought still breathing to the fire and roasted.

**9:4** While the vapor of the burning spread out all around, the brothers together with the mother urged one another to die nobly, saying in these words:

**9:5** The Lord God sees all things, and without question he has true compassion on us, even as Moses declared in his song, which bore witness against the people saying, And he will have compassion on his servants.

**9:6** When the first brother had died in this way, they brought the second for sport; and when they had torn off the skin of his head, they asked him, Will you eat before your whole body is punished limb by limb?

**9:7** He answered in the language of his fathers and said to them: No!

**9:8** Therefore he endured the next tortures in succession.

**9:9** When the second also had died in a worthy manner, the third was brought and was asked the same question.

**9:10** He answered: I will not deny the blessed law of God, nor will I betray the noble deed of my brothers. I will endure it all.

**9:11** And when he had been racked and the flesh of his arms had been torn off, he was brought to the wheel while they called out to him: Renounce your impiety and we will have mercy on you!

**9:12** But he answered: Your wheel is not so powerful that it can take from me the eternal life. Cut my body; for you cannot touch my soul with all your machines of torture.

**9:13** When Antiochus and his attendants saw that the youth could not be persuaded, they had him brought to the fire while still alive, commanding his brothers and the mother also to be spectators at the fire.

**9:14** But the mother and the brothers encouraged one another to die for the law, saying to one another in the ancestral tongue:

**9:15** The Lord God looks down on us and in truth has compassion on us as Moses declared in the song of testimony saying, And he will have compassion on his servants.

**9:16** And when the first of the brothers had thus died, the others also each in turn declared the same courage.

**9:17** The first, having borne his suffering as far as death, said: I will endure every kind of pain for the sake of the soul that has hope of God.

**9:18** The second said: Do you not think, murderer of men, that in proportion as you torment us you will be tormented the more?

**9:19** The third one, when he was commanded to put out his tongue, quickly stretched it out and fearlessly extended his hands saying:

**9:20** From heaven I received these; and for the sake of his laws I disdain them; and from him I hope to receive them again.

**9:21** So that even the king and those with him were amazed at the young man's spirit, how he regarded the sufferings as though they were nothing.

**9:22** When he too was dead, they tortured the fourth in the same way.

**9:23** And when he was near to death he said: It is better for those who die at God's hand to cherish hope of a divine resurrection; as for you, there will be no resurrection to life.

**9:24** After this they brought forward the fifth and maltreated him.

**9:25** Looking at the king he said: Since you have authority among men, you do as you please, though you are corruptible. But do not suppose that God has forsaken our race.

**9:26** Just keep on, and see how his great power will torture you and your seed.
